newsitem.title: UK: Portillo accuses Blair of weather vane politics.
newsitem.headline: Portillo accuses Blair of weather vane politics.

text.p: Labour leader Tony Blair only says what British voters want to hear, Defence Secretary Michael Portillo said on Wednesday.
In a speech on the fringe of the ruling Conservative Party's annual conference, Portillo lambasted Blair for his weather vane politics and the Labour party for its ties with trade unions.
"Mr Blair has made a career of equivocation and ambiguity, and steers by the compass of the focus group and the opinion poll to a horizon no more distant than the general election," Portillo said.
In a back-handed compliment, he added: "For the moment he has developed to a high degree the skill of finding out what people want to hear, then saying it."
Labour enjoys a commanding 20-point poll lead over the Conservatives in the run-up to the election, which must be held by May.

"Mr Blair is an unusual case. He recognises that his only hope of winning office is to sound as though he had become a Conservative. The danger from new Labour is that it has adopted a sort of Conservative language by way of disguise," Portillo said.
